images.title: Lift on its side
images.purpose: Show that turning the endless lift a quarter turn gives a number line, with up as right and down as left.
images.composition: Vertical lift shaft on the left, a single curved arrow in the middle, a horizontal number line on the right, with wide space between the three.
images.exact_structure: Left: one tall thin vertical shaft in grey #6B7280 with 5 equal floor marks, the middle mark labelled 0, the top mark teal #0072B2 and the bottom mark amber #E69F00. Middle: one quarter-turn arrow in reddish purple #CC79A7. Right: one horizontal line with 5 equally spaced ticks, the middle tick labelled 0, the right end tick teal and the left end tick amber, and arrowheads at both ends. Exactly 1 shaft, 1 arrow, 1 line.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Turn the lift on its side and it is a number line.
images.description: A vertical lift shaft with 5 floors, a quarter-turn arrow, and a horizontal number line with 5 ticks where up matches right and down matches left.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the top floor and find where it lands on the line.

image_decisions.why: The lift-to-number-line match is a picture idea; one clean turn picture carries it.
